inferences.claim: the callee pops 8 byte(s) of stack arguments

ECX carries the receiver: 0x00a98400 is slot 6 of the vptr-backed vftable at 0x01458788, so it is a virtual member of some class and every virtual call that reaches it indexes the vptr through the object address; the body reads its incoming ECX before writing it, and a body that reads a register the vtable dispatch delivered uses the object, so the receiver is in ECX. The callee pops its own stack arguments, which is the COM / __stdcall interface form, and that is the one shape in which a virtual member takes its receiver from the first popped stack word instead -- a body in that form never reads its incoming ECX, which is why this body reading it is what decides the two apart
calling convention is __thiscall: the callee pops the stack arguments, which rules out cdecl and fastcall, and the receiver arrives in ECX
entry slot 0 is not written through a pointer
the return value is carried in XMM0: an x87 or SSE instruction appears in the body

sret.basis: entry slot 0 is not written through a pointer; DERIVED absence is weak, a struct filled through another alias would be missed
